basis: Scalp aplasia and terminal limb defects define AOS; severe developmental and brain abnormalities reported in ~50%. Optic atrophy 3/12; ocular damage not securely above 30%.
Psychotic and depressive disorder without defining damage to an organ axis.
Benign glandular proliferation confined to the breast, which has no axis.
Giant bullous emphysema directly and irreversibly destroys pulmonary parenchyma.
Drug-resistant mycobacterial infection; pulmonary infection directly damages lungs in the large majority, roughly 80% or more.
Hepatitis A virus directly causes acute hepatic inflammation; arthralgia does not establish joint damage.
Congenital linear growth restriction is the defining physical abnormality, with birth length below the third percentile in 5/5. Feeding difficulty alone is not gastrointestinal damage.
Factor V isoform-related coagulation disorder causing abnormal bleeding.
Perforating keratinizing skin disease; diabetes, renal disease, liver abnormalities and heart failure are associated separate conditions.
Progressive neurodegeneration causes movement abnormalities, cognitive impairment and cerebral atrophy; no established common blood dysfunction.
Developmental impairment and epilepsy define the syndrome. Cardiac, hearing and structural skeletal abnormalities are occasional, below 30%.
Premalignant disorders of hematopoietic cells; lymphoma or immune dysfunction does not apply across this umbrella.
Complete congenital cryptophthalmia affects eyelid formation and the underlying eye.
Arterial dissection and medial degeneration together with multiple cutaneous lentigines define the syndrome.
Cleft lip and palate are defining congenital abnormalities of the mouth; other TP63-associated disorders are not assumed.
Glomus-cell vascular neoplasm with dilated venous channels, typically arising in skin and subcutaneous tissue.
Lissencephaly and cerebellar hypoplasia define the brain disorder; fixed congenital joint contractures occur in 10/10 annotated patients.
Immunodeficiency with HLH-like disease; hepatic injury 12/15 and pulmonary hemorrhage 6/15. Neurologic involvement (~47%) omitted by cap; renal insufficiency 4/15 is below 30%.
Developmental impairment and structural brain abnormalities define disease; ankle contractures reported in 2/5 (~40%). Recurrent respiratory infections do not establish chronic lung injury.
Fragile X syndrome subtype defined by neurodevelopmental impairment; no evidence supports additional common organ damage.
Disordered penile vascular inflow or outflow causes persistent erection; classified as peripheral vascular disease. Hematologic and neurologic causes are separate conditions.
Glioma originates in and directly occupies brainstem tissue.
Inherited metabolic disorders causing cerebellar dysfunction; additional organ involvement varies across subtypes and is not established across the group.
Tumor originates in the ileum. Neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish endocrine gland disease; metastases and carcinoid syndrome are not assumed.
Ventricular electrical dysfunction causes loss of effective cardiac pumping; secondary hypoxic organ injuries are not intrinsic defining involvement.
